set.title: Fictional bookshop · shared manual and agent trial
set.context: Fictional usability trial only. A bookshop is considering paid workshops next quarter. Five staff-hours a week are available; demand and budget are unknown. No empirical claims or recommendation.

problem.situation: A fictional bookshop is considering paid workshops. Demand and budget are unknown.
problem.desiredChange: Earn extra contribution next quarter without disrupting the shop.
problem.constraints: At most five staff-hours per week; budget still to clarify.

set.nextQuestion: What would count as enough extra contribution to make a workshop worth the effort?

editNodes.label: Could paid workshops be worthwhile?
editNodes.notes: Initial issue tree: willingness to pay, incremental economics, and operational feasibility. These are decision conditions, not a claim of statistical independence or an exhaustive causal partition. Demand influences revenue; staffing influences costs.

addNodes.label: Would revenue cover the extra costs?
Can it fit within five staff-hours a week?
Extra contribution
addNodes.notes: For next quarter, extra contribution (GBP) = workshop ticket revenue (GBP) minus avoidable extra workshop costs (GBP). All inputs are unknown. Existing shop rent is excluded unless workshops change it; staff time and displaced shop activity need explicit treatment.

addNodes.label: Ticket revenue
addNodes.notes: Add workshop ticket revenue in GBP over the quarter. No attendance or price is assumed.

addNodes.label: Avoidable extra costs
addNodes.notes: Subtract extra costs attributable to workshops over the quarter, in GBP. Include setup and delivery; avoid counting the same staff cost twice.

addNodes.label: A practical workshop could attract paying readers
addNodes.notes: Proposed explanation of potential demand, not a fact. Topic, audience, price and booking commitment need to be specified. A waitlist alone would not establish willingness to pay.

addNodes.label: Check interest at a stated price
addNodes.notes: Proposed research task only: first inspect any relevant existing booking evidence. If inadequate, ask prospective readers about a concrete workshop and price; distinguish interest from paid commitment. No research or event has been launched.
